insights: The standard-normal MGF g(t)=exp(t^2/2) satisfies the first-order ODE g'=t*g; this single ODE drives a parity-preserving moment recursion.

Mathlib's iteratedDeriv_mgf_zero gives E[X^n] = g^{(n)}(0), so the whole moment computation happens on the smooth function exp(t^2/2) with no measure-theoretic estimates (integrableExpSet_id_gaussianReal = R supplies the interior hypothesis).

A Leibniz product rule against the linear factor t, (t*f)^{(n+1)}(x)=x*f^{(n+1)}(x)+(n+1)*f^{(n)}(x), evaluated at x=0 kills the x-term and yields recursion coefficient (n+1): g^{(n+2)}(0)=(n+1)*g^{(n)}(0).
The recursion is index-parity-preserving, so one lemma produces both even moments (2k-1)!! and vanishing odd moments — closing both open strands of the parent's OQ-01 at once.
Product form prod_{i<k}(2i+1) is the natural recursion output; identifying it with Nat.doubleFactorial (2k-1) is a separate arithmetic induction (handled at k=0 by the (2*0-1)=0 truncation, 0!!=1).
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has the Gaussian MGF and iteratedDeriv_mgf_zero but no ready-made closed form for the general Gaussian even moment (2k-1)!!; this file supplies it.
No general iterated-Leibniz rule specialized to a linear factor was readily reusable; iteratedDeriv_id_mul fills that locally.
